claim: Antibody production following vaccination can provide protective immunity to subsequent infection by pathogens such as influenza viruses.
source: Antibody production following vaccination can provide protective immunity to subsequent infection by pathogens such as influenza viruses.
evidence: This is a general statement about vaccination and immunity that is part of established scientific knowledge in immunology.

claim: Formation of circulating T follicular helper (cTfh) cells was associated with high-titre antibody responses.
source: Here, by studying the breadth of anti-haemagglutinin (HA) IgG, serum cytokines, and B and T cell responses by flow cytometry before and after influenza vaccination, we show that formation of circulating T follicular helper (cTfh) cells was associated with high-titre antibody responses.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from flow cytometry analysis of immune responses before and after vaccination.

claim: HA-specific cTfh cells can derive from pre-existing memory CD4+ T cells.
source: Using Major Histocompatability Complex (MHC) class II tetramers, we demonstrate that HA-specific cTfh cells can derive from pre-existing memory CD4+ T cells and have a diverse T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using MHC class II tetramers to track T cells.

claim: HA-specific cTfh cells have a diverse T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire.
source: Using Major Histocompatability Complex (MHC) class II tetramers, we demonstrate that HA-specific cTfh cells can derive from pre-existing memory CD4+ T cells and have a diverse T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing analysis.

claim: In older people, the differentiation of HA-specific cells into cTfh cells was impaired.
source: In older people, the differentiation of HA-specific cells into cTfh cells was impaired.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing younger and older cohorts.

claim: The age-dependent defect in cTfh cell formation was not due to a contraction of the TCR repertoire.
source: This age-dependent defect in cTfh cell formation was not due to a contraction of the TCR repertoire, but rather was linked with an increased inflammatory gene signature in cTfh cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by TCR sequencing data showing no difference in TCR diversity between age groups.

claim: The age-dependent defect in cTfh cell formation was linked with an increased inflammatory gene signature in cTfh cells.
source: This age-dependent defect in cTfh cell formation was not due to a contraction of the TCR repertoire, but rather was linked with an increased inflammatory gene signature in cTfh cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data showing increased inflammatory gene expression in older individuals.

claim: Strategies that temporarily dampen inflammation at the time of vaccination may be a viable strategy to boost optimal antibody generation upon immunisation of older people.
source: Together, this suggests that strategies that temporarily dampen inflammation at the time of vaccination may be a viable strategy to boost optimal antibody generation upon immunisation of older people.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the observed association between inflammation and poor vaccine responses.

claim: The seasonal influenza vaccine needs to be administered each year in order to provide protection against the most prevalent circulating influenza strains.
source: The seasonal influenza vaccine needs to be administered each year in order to provide protection against the most prevalent circulating influenza strains, but its efficacy typically ranges from 40 to 80% even when the vaccine is antigenically matched to circulating viruses.
evidence: This is established knowledge about influenza vaccination practices.

claim: The efficacy of seasonal influenza vaccine typically ranges from 40 to 80% even when the vaccine is antigenically matched to circulating viruses.
source: The seasonal influenza vaccine needs to be administered each year in order to provide protection against the most prevalent circulating influenza strains, but its efficacy typically ranges from 40 to 80% even when the vaccine is antigenically matched to circulating viruses.
evidence: This is established knowledge about influenza vaccine efficacy.

claim: Inefficacy of seasonal influenza vaccine contributes to millions of severe influenza cases and hundreds of thousands of deaths globally.
source: This inefficacy contributes to millions of severe influenza cases and hundreds of thousands of deaths globally (Iuliano et al., 2018), which could be potentially prevented by a more effective vaccine.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Antibodies against the influenza surface glycoprotein haemagglutinin (HA) are capable of limiting infection.
source: Antibodies against the influenza surface glycoprotein haemagglutinin (HA) are capable of limiting infection, and anti-HA antibody titres and inhibitory activity are the most commonly used correlate of protection (Hobson et al., 1972).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Anti-HA antibody titres and inhibitory activity are the most commonly used correlate of protection.
source: Antibodies against the influenza surface glycoprotein haemagglutinin (HA) are capable of limiting infection, and anti-HA antibody titres and inhibitory activity are the most commonly used correlate of protection (Hobson et al., 1972).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The human antibody response to influenza vaccination is highly variable.
source: The human antibody response to influenza vaccination is highly variable, but what causes this inter-individual variation is not well understood.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of influenza vaccination.

claim: Genetics can account for less than 20% of the variation in antibody responses to influenza vaccination.
source: Twin studies estimate that genetics can account for less than 20% of the variation in antibody responses to influenza vaccination, implicating non-heritable factors as key contributing influences (Brodin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to twin studies.

claim: Age, sex, chronic viral infections, and non-communicable diseases have all been reported to influence antibody titre following vaccination.
source: Age, sex, chronic viral infections, and non-communicable diseases have all been reported to influence antibody titre following vaccination (Frost, 2020; Furman et al., 2015; Giefing-Kröll et al., 2015; Hill et al., 2020; Nakaya et al., 2015; Stebegg et al., 2020), but how these various factors impact immune responses to vaccination have yet to be fully unravelled.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The generation of protective humoral immunity is supported by CD4+ helper T cells.
source: The generation of protective humoral immunity is supported by CD4+ helper T cells (Vinuesa et al., 2016), which, like neutralising antibodies, are correlates of protection for influenza infection (Wilkinson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to published literature.

claim: CD4+ helper T cells, like neutralising antibodies, are correlates of protection for influenza infection.
source: The generation of protective humoral immunity is supported by CD4+ helper T cells (Vinuesa et al., 2016), which, like neutralising antibodies, are correlates of protection for influenza infection (Wilkinson et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: IgG levels increased against all measured HA proteins from the vaccine influenza strains at d7 and d42.
source: IgG levels increased against all measured HA proteins from the vaccine influenza strains at d7 and d42 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: IgG titres to 31 out of 32 HA proteins (96%) were altered at d42 relative to baseline (d0).
source: From our panel of 32 HA proteins, IgG titres to 31 (96%) were altered at d42 relative to baseline (d0), with the greatest fold changes observed for HA strains contained in the TIV.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Luminex assays.

claim: The greatest fold changes in IgG titres were observed for HA strains contained in the TIV.
source: From our panel of 32 HA proteins, IgG titres to 31 (96%) were altered at d42 relative to baseline (d0), with the greatest fold changes observed for HA strains contained in the TIV.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Luminex assays.

claim: Vaccine-induced IgG responses were able to partially cross-react across multiple influenza strains.
source: These data indicate that vaccine-induced IgG responses were able to partially cross-react across multiple influenza strains (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing IgG responses to multiple HA strains.

claim: The increase in anti-HA antibody titre was coupled with an increase in haemagglutination inhibitory antibodies to A.Cali09.
source: The increase in anti-HA antibody titre was coupled with an increase in haemagglutination inhibitory antibodies to A.Cali09, the one influenza A strain contained in the TIVs that was shared across the two cohorts and showed a positive correlation with the A.Cali09 IgG titres measured by Luminex assay (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from HAI assays and correlation analysis.

claim: A.Cali09 HAI titres showed a positive correlation with the A.Cali09 IgG titres measured by Luminex assay.
source: The increase in anti-HA antibody titre was coupled with an increase in haemagglutination inhibitory antibodies to A.Cali09, the one influenza A strain contained in the TIVs that was shared across the two cohorts and showed a positive correlation with the A.Cali09 IgG titres measured by Luminex assay (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing correlation between two antibody measurements.

claim: Four cytokines were upregulated (CXCL13, BCMA, APRIL, and Osteopontin) at d7 post-vaccination.
source: Our analysis of eight cytokines by Luminex identified that four cytokines were upregulated (CXCL13, BCMA, APRIL, and Osteopontin) and two were downregulated (BAFF and TWEAK) at d7 post-vaccination (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Luminex cytokine assays.

claim: Two cytokines were downregulated (BAFF and TWEAK) at d7 post-vaccination.
source: Our analysis of eight cytokines by Luminex identified that four cytokines were upregulated (CXCL13, BCMA, APRIL, and Osteopontin) and two were downregulated (BAFF and TWEAK) at d7 post-vaccination (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Luminex cytokine assays.

claim: The frequency of cTfh cells (CD45RA-CXCR5+PD1++) was increased on d7.
source: We did not detect alterations in the frequency of any B cell subsets in either cohort by flow cytometry; however, the frequency of cTfh cells (CD45RA-CXCR5+PD1++) was increased on d7 (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 5), a population that we and others have previously shown share transcriptional and clonal similarity with germinal centre Tfh cells (Brenna et al., 2020; Heit et al., 2017; Hill et al., 2019; Locci et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from flow cytometry.

claim: cTfh cells share transcriptional and clonal similarity with germinal centre Tfh cells.
source: We did not detect alterations in the frequency of any B cell subsets in either cohort by flow cytometry; however, the frequency of cTfh cells (CD45RA-CXCR5+PD1++) was increased on d7 (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 5), a population that we and others have previously shown share transcriptional and clonal similarity with germinal centre Tfh cells (Brenna et al., 2020; Heit et al., 2017; Hill et al., 2019; Locci et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature including the authors' own work.

claim: The expression of ICOS on cTfh cells was increased on d7.
source: Furthermore, the expression of ICOS on cTfh cells was increased on d7, confirming the cTfh population is an activated effector population that forms in response to vaccination (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from flow cytometry.

claim: The cTfh population is an activated effector population that forms in response to vaccination.
source: Furthermore, the expression of ICOS on cTfh cells was increased on d7, confirming the cTfh population is an activated effector population that forms in response to vaccination (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing increased ICOS expression.

claim: Tetramer-binding antigen-experienced CD4+CD45RA- (Tet+) T cells showed the largest fold change increase after vaccination of any parameter measured.
source: Tetramer-binding antigen-experienced CD4+CD45RA- (Tet+) T cells showed the largest fold change increase after vaccination of any parameter measured (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from tetramer staining and flow cytometry.

claim: Tet+ cells were detected in all individuals before vaccination.
source: Tet+ cells were detected in all individuals before vaccination and expanded a median of 5–11-fold between d0 and d7 in both cohorts (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from tetramer staining.

claim: Tet+ cells expanded a median of 5–11-fold between d0 and d7 in both cohorts.
source: Tet+ cells were detected in all individuals before vaccination and expanded a median of 5–11-fold between d0 and d7 in both cohorts (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from tetramer staining and flow cytometry.

claim: HA-specific T cells upregulated ICOS after immunisation, indicating that they have been activated by vaccination.
source: These antigen-specific T cells had upregulated ICOS after immunisation, indicating that they have been activated by vaccination (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing increased ICOS expression.

claim: A median of one third of HA-specific T cells upregulated the Tfh markers CXCR5 and PD1 on d7 after immunisation.
source: In addition, a median of one third of HA-specific T cells upregulated the Tfh markers CXCR5 and PD1 on d7 after immunisation (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from flow cytometry.

claim: The majority of Tet+ cTfh cells expressed CXCR3.
source: The majority of Tet+ cTfh cells expressed CXCR3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6C and D), consistent with the 'Th1' skew in the total CD4+ T cell (Yang et al., 2013) and cTfh cell response to influenza vaccination (Bentebibel et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from flow cytometry and is consistent with cited literature.

claim: Seasonal influenza vaccination increases anti-HA IgG titres.
source: Therefore, seasonal influenza vaccination increases anti-HA IgG titres, induces a cTfh response, and promotes the expansion and differentiation of HA-specific CD4+ T cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental data presented.

claim: Seasonal influenza vaccination induces a cTfh response.
source: Therefore, seasonal influenza vaccination increases anti-HA IgG titres, induces a cTfh response, and promotes the expansion and differentiation of HA-specific CD4+ T cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental data presented.

claim: Seasonal influenza vaccination promotes the expansion and differentiation of HA-specific CD4+ T cells.
source: Therefore, seasonal influenza vaccination increases anti-HA IgG titres, induces a cTfh response, and promotes the expansion and differentiation of HA-specific CD4+ T cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental data presented.

claim: Pre-existing antibody titres have been linked with diminished responses to subsequent vaccination.
source: Pre-existing antibody titres have been linked with diminished responses to subsequent vaccination (Tsang et al., 2014; Sasaki et al., 2008; Bucasas et al., 2011), but while we observed a slight negative correlation at d0 in support of this, the relationship was not statistically significant for any of the Flu HA Luminex or A.Cali09 HAI titres (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature, though the authors' own data did not show statistical significance.

claim: The IgG responses to a range of HA proteins from different influenza strains correlated strongly with A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0).
source: In contrast, the IgG responses to a range of HA proteins from different influenza strains correlated strongly with A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0), indicating that those individuals with large vaccine-induced IgG responses also developed cross-reactive antibodies against multiple strains (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from correlation analysis.

claim: Individuals with large vaccine-induced IgG responses also developed cross-reactive antibodies against multiple strains.
source: In contrast, the IgG responses to a range of HA proteins from different influenza strains correlated strongly with A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0), indicating that those individuals with large vaccine-induced IgG responses also developed cross-reactive antibodies against multiple strains (Figure 2B).

claim: Changes between d0 and d7 in serum BCMA were positively correlated with A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0) responses in both cohorts.
source: Changes between d0 and d7 in serum BCMA were positively correlated, and BAFF negatively correlated with A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0) responses, in both cohorts (Figure 2C and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from correlation analysis.

claim: Changes between d0 and d7 in serum BAFF were negatively correlated with A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0) responses in both cohorts.
source: Changes between d0 and d7 in serum BCMA were positively correlated, and BAFF negatively correlated with A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0) responses, in both cohorts (Figure 2C and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from correlation analysis.

claim: The frequency of B cell subsets, including antibody-secreting cells at d7, was not associated with d42 A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0).
source: The frequency of B cell subsets, including antibody-secreting cells at d7, was not associated with d42 A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0), whereas total cTfh cell frequency correlated with antibodies in both cohorts (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from correlation analysis.

claim: Total cTfh cell frequency correlated with antibodies in both cohorts.
source: The frequency of B cell subsets, including antibody-secreting cells at d7, was not associated with d42 A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0), whereas total cTfh cell frequency correlated with antibodies in both cohorts (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from correlation analysis.

claim: A reproducible positive correlation was observed between A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0) and HA-specific cTfh cells.
source: A reproducible positive correlation was observed between A.Cali09 IgG (d42-d0) and HA-specific cTfh cells (Figure 2D and E), but not consistently for total Tet+ CD4+ T cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from correlation analysis across both cohorts.

claim: The differentiation of antigen-specific Tfh cells is more relevant for antibody responses than the overall frequency of antigen-specific helper T cells.
source: This indicates that the differentiation of antigen-specific Tfh cells is more relevant for antibody responses than the overall frequency of antigen-specific helper T cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the correlation data showing stronger association with cTfh cells than total Tet+ cells.

claim: Expanded clones were observed on d7.
source: Expanded clones were observed on d7 (Figure 3B), resulting in a decrease in the diversity of the TCR repertoire at d7 relative to d0 (Figure 3C) and an increase in the number of co-dominant TCRβ clonotypes within the HA-specific TCR repertoire of each individual (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing.

claim: There was a decrease in the diversity of the TCR repertoire at d7 relative to d0.
source: Expanded clones were observed on d7 (Figure 3B), resulting in a decrease in the diversity of the TCR repertoire at d7 relative to d0 (Figure 3C) and an increase in the number of co-dominant TCRβ clonotypes within the HA-specific TCR repertoire of each individual (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing and diversity analysis.

claim: There was an increase in the number of co-dominant TCRβ clonotypes within the HA-specific TCR repertoire of each individual at d7.
source: Expanded clones were observed on d7 (Figure 3B), resulting in a decrease in the diversity of the TCR repertoire at d7 relative to d0 (Figure 3C) and an increase in the number of co-dominant TCRβ clonotypes within the HA-specific TCR repertoire of each individual (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing.

claim: TCRβ clonotypes were recalled from the d0 memory CD4+ T cell pool into the cTfh cell response at d7 in 10 out of 15 individuals.
source: Analysis of paired samples that were sequenced at both d0 and d7 demonstrated that TCRβ clonotypes were recalled from the d0 memory CD4+ T cell pool into the cTfh cell response at d7 in 10 out of 15 individuals (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing of paired samples.

claim: Recalled TCRβ clones represented a median of 25% of the overall TCR repertoire at d7.
source: Recalled TCRβ clones represented a median of 25% of the overall TCR repertoire at d7 (Figure 3G) and were more likely to have been more abundant at d0 compared to clones only detected at d0 (Figure 3H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing analysis.

claim: Recalled TCRβ clones were more likely to have been more abundant at d0 compared to clones only detected at d0.
source: Recalled TCRβ clones represented a median of 25% of the overall TCR repertoire at d7 (Figure 3G) and were more likely to have been more abundant at d0 compared to clones only detected at d0 (Figure 3H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing analysis.

claim: Public clonotypes were present in 18 out 20 cTfh Tet+ samples at d7.
source: Identical TCRβ sequences between two or more individuals, or 'public clonotypes', were present in 18 out 20 cTfh Tet+ samples at d7 and represented a median of 10% of the total response (total of 32 distinct public TCR sequences, Figure 3I and J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing analysis.

claim: Public clonotypes represented a median of 10% of the total response at d7.
source: Identical TCRβ sequences between two or more individuals, or 'public clonotypes', were present in 18 out 20 cTfh Tet+ samples at d7 and represented a median of 10% of the total response (total of 32 distinct public TCR sequences, Figure 3I and J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing analysis.

claim: Only four public clonotypes were shared across seven individuals at d0.
source: In contrast, only four public clonotypes were shared across seven individuals at d0.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing analysis.

claim: There was a tendency for public clonotypes to preferentially use particular TCRBV and TCRBJ gene combinations.
source: There was a tendency for public clonotypes to preferentially use particular TCRBV and TCRBJ gene combinations (Figure 3K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TCR sequencing analysis.

claim: The vaccine-induced cTfh response to A.Cali09 involves reactivation of existing memory CD4+ T cells.
source: These results demonstrate that the vaccine-induced cTfh response to A.Cali09 involves reactivation of existing memory CD4+ T cells, and that common responses between individuals are a prevalent part of the cTfh cell response.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the TCR sequencing data showing recalled clonotypes.

claim: Common responses between individuals are a prevalent part of the cTfh cell response.
source: These results demonstrate that the vaccine-induced cTfh response to A.Cali09 involves reactivation of existing memory CD4+ T cells, and that common responses between individuals are a prevalent part of the cTfh cell response.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the TCR sequencing data showing public clonotypes.

claim: HA-specific cTfh cells that form 7 days after vaccination clustered distinctly from their d0 Tet+ precursors cells by principal component analysis (PCA) for both cohorts.
source: HA-specific cTfh cells that form 7 days after vaccination clustered distinctly from their d0 Tet+ precursors cells by principal component analysis (PCA) for both cohorts (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNA sequencing and PCA analysis.

claim: 684 genes were differentially expressed (DE) in Tet+ cTfh cells compared to d0 Tet+ cells across both cohorts.
source: 684 genes were differentially expressed (DE) in Tet+ cTfh cells compared to d0 Tet+ cells across both cohorts (DESeq2 log2FC > 0.5, FDR p-value<0.1, Source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNA sequencing and differential expression analysis.

claim: 147 of the DE genes in Tet+ cTfh cells shared the same expression pattern with genes up- or downregulated in germinal centre Tfh signature.
source: 147 of the DE genes in Tet+ cTfh cells shared the same expression pattern with genes up- or downregulated in germinal centre Tfh signature, termed 'Tfh genes'.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNA sequencing and comparison with lymph node Tfh cell signature.

claim: Tet+ cTfh cells upregulated key Tfh cell transcription factors MAF and TOX2.
source: These included upregulation of key Tfh cell transcription factors MAF and TOX2, and downregulation of several cytokine and chemokine receptors such as IL7R, IL2RA, and CCR6 (Figure 4B and C, Source data 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNA sequencing.

claim: Tet+ cTfh cells downregulated several cytokine and chemokine receptors such as IL7R, IL2RA, and CCR6.
source: These included upregulation of key Tfh cell transcription factors MAF and TOX2, and downregulation of several cytokine and chemokine receptors such as IL7R, IL2RA, and CCR6 (Figure 4B and C, Source data 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNA sequencing.

claim: Tet+ cTfh cells downregulated CXCR4, a chemokine receptor that is important for lymph node homing.
source: This list included the downregulation of CXCR4, a chemokine receptor that is important for lymph node homing consistent with the blood localisation of the cTfh cells (Okada et al., 2002), and upregulation of the interferon-gamma-inducible gene GBP2.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNA sequencing and is consistent with cited literature.

claim: Tet+ cTfh cells upregulated the interferon-gamma-inducible gene GBP2.
source: This list included the downregulation of CXCR4, a chemokine receptor that is important for lymph node homing consistent with the blood localisation of the cTfh cells (Okada et al., 2002), and upregulation of the interferon-gamma-inducible gene GBP2.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNA sequencing.

claim: Tet+ cTfh cells share features of a transcriptional profile with lymph node Tfh cells.
source: This gene-level analysis indicated that Tet+ cTfh cells share features of a transcriptional profile with lymph node Tfh cells, while also expressing genes specific either to the Th1-skew in the Tfh response to influenza vaccination or to circulation in the blood.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the RNA sequencing data comparing cTfh cells with lymph node Tfh cells.

claim: Ten gene sets were differentially modulated in d7 Tet+ Tfh cells compared to d0 in both cohorts.
source: Ten gene sets were differentially modulated in d7 Tet+ Tfh cells compared to d0 in both cohorts, eight (80%) of which were also enriched in lymph node germinal centre Tfh cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from gene set enrichment analysis.

claim: Eight out of ten differentially modulated gene sets (80%) were also enriched in lymph node germinal centre Tfh cells.
source: Ten gene sets were differentially modulated in d7 Tet+ Tfh cells compared to d0 in both cohorts, eight (80%) of which were also enriched in lymph node germinal centre Tfh cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from gene set enrichment analysis.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from gene set enrichment analysis and is consistent with cited literature.

claim: IL-2 is a cytokine known to inhibit Tfh differentiation.

evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Tet+ cTfh cells showed upregulation of oxidative phosphorylation.
source: These 'Tfh gene sets' included the downregulation of several cytokine pathways including IL-2 signalling, a cytokine known to inhibit Tfh differentiation (Ballesteros-Tato et al., 2012; DiToro et al., 2018), and the upregulation of oxidative phosphorylation, a metabolic process known to be elevated in Tfh cells (Figure 4E; Dong et al., 2019; Ray et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from gene set enrichment analysis and is consistent with cited literature.

claim: Oxidative phosphorylation is a metabolic process known to be elevated in Tfh cells.
source: These 'Tfh gene sets' included the downregulation of several cytokine pathways including IL-2 signalling, a cytokine known to inhibit Tfh differentiation (Ballesteros-Tato et al., 2012; DiToro et al., 2018), and the upregulation of oxidative phosphorylation, a metabolic process known to be elevated in Tfh cells (Figure 4E; Dong et al., 2019; Ray et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Seasonal influenza vaccination recalls antigen-specific memory CD4+ T cells and promotes their differentiation into Tfh cells with similarity to lymph node GC Tfh cells.
source: Overall, our analysis demonstrates that seasonal influenza vaccination recalls antigen-specific memory CD4+ T cells and promotes their differentiation into Tfh cells with similarity to lymph node GC Tfh cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the RNA sequencing and TCR analysis data.

claim: Older individuals showed lower HA-specific IgG responses compared to 18–36 year olds for all the vaccine strains measured.
source: We compared our cohorts of 18–36 year olds with that of individuals over 65 years old in the same vaccination years (Figure 5A, cohort 1 median 69 years old, cohort 2 median 73.43 years old) and observed that older individuals showed lower HA-specific IgG responses compared to 18–36 year olds for all the vaccine strains measured (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing antibody responses between age groups.

claim: There was no pre-vaccination difference in trajectory values between the age groups.
source: There was no pre-vaccination difference in trajectory values between the age groups, indicating that ageing did not impact the baseline status for the immune parameters involved in the vaccination response (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from diffusion pseudotime analysis.

claim: Over 65 year olds failed to progress along the vaccination trajectory to the same extent as their 18–36-year-old counterparts.
source: In contrast, over 65 year olds failed to progress along the vaccination trajectory to the same extent as their 18–36-year-old counterparts (Figure 5D), indicating a failure to appropriately respond to vaccination.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from diffusion pseudotime analysis.

claim: 11 immune parameters correlated with the vaccination trajectory values.
source: 11 immune parameters correlated with the vaccination trajectory values, including antibody responses to the vaccination strains, cTfh cells, HA-specific T cells, and diminished serum BAFF (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from correlation analysis.

claim: In over 65 year olds there is a failure to fully engage the adaptive immune system in response to vaccination compared to younger individuals.
source: These results indicate that in over 65 year olds there is a failure to fully engage the adaptive immune system in response to vaccination compared to younger individuals.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the vaccination trajectory analysis.

claim: Older individuals had higher titres of IgG to several HA proteins from different influenza A strains at d0.
source: Older individuals had higher titres of IgG to several HA proteins from different influenza A strains at d0; however, no difference was seen in IgG or HAI titre levels for the influenza strains in the vaccines administered to our cohorts (Figure 5F), suggesting that age-dependent differences in pre-existing antibodies to the vaccine strain do not account for the diminished response.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Luminex assays comparing age groups.

claim: No difference was seen in IgG or HAI titre levels for the influenza strains in the vaccines at d0 between age groups.
source: Older individuals had higher titres of IgG to several HA proteins from different influenza A strains at d0; however, no difference was seen in IgG or HAI titre levels for the influenza strains in the vaccines administered to our cohorts (Figure 5F), suggesting that age-dependent differences in pre-existing antibodies to the vaccine strain do not account for the diminished response.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Luminex and HAI assays.

claim: Age-dependent differences in pre-existing antibodies to the vaccine strain do not account for the diminished response in older individuals.

claim: IL-2 is a cytokine produced by T cells early after T cell activation that promotes clonal expansion and favours a Th1 cell fate at the expense of Tfh cell differentiation.
source: IL-2 is a cytokine produced by T cells early after T cell activation that promotes clonal expansion and favours a Th1 cell fate at the expense of Tfh cell differentiation (Ballesteros-Tato et al., 2012; Ray et al., 2015), in line with the negative relationship observed here between cTfh cell differentiation and the response to IL-2 in those cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Tfh cells are reported to be IL-2 producers as a consequence of heightened TCR signalling.
source: Tfh cells are reported to be IL-2 producers as a consequence of heightened TCR signalling, and whilst they typically do not respond to IL-2, they provide a source of this cytokine to support non-Tfh cells (DiToro et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Enhanced IL-2 production in vivo results in fewer Tfh cells in secondary lymphoid organs.
source: Here, we have used genetically modified mice to demonstrate that enhanced IL-2 production in vivo results in fewer Tfh cells in secondary lymphoid organs, demonstrating that aberrantly produced IL-2 has negative consequences for Tfh cell formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetically modified mouse studies.

claim: TNF is necessary for the formation of primary B cell follicles and follicular dendritic cell networks that underpin the formation of germinal centres.

evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Serum TNF levels and TNF production from memory B cells have been reported to increase with age.
source: While in our study serum concentrations for both TNF and IL-2 were below the limit of detection in most samples, serum TNF levels and TNF production from memory B cells have been reported to increase with age (Carr et al., 2016; Frasca et al., 2014), suggesting that our TNF signature in cTfh cells may result from paracrine sources .
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Persistence of TNF signalling in cTfh cells is linked to poor vaccine responses.
source: Therefore, while it is unclear whether TNF acts directly on T cells to impair Tfh differentiation or survival, or has a broader effect on lymphoid organ architecture, our data indicate that persistence of TNF signalling in cTfh cells is linked to poor vaccine responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data showing associations between TNF signatures and poor responses.

claim: Older people are more likely to become seriously ill, or die, after COVID-19 infection.
source: The need to develop effective vaccines that are effective in all age groups has been emphasised by the COVID19 pandemic, in which older people are more likely to become seriously ill, or die, after infection (Verity et al., 2020).
